newsitem.title: USA: U.S. energy prices pause on ACCESS after rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. energy prices pause on ACCESS after rally.

text.p: U.S. energy futures paused in thin after-hours trade on Wednesday after a second straight day of record highs for heating oil, which left traders wondering where the contract would peak.
"People aren't seeing any room for closure until 75/76 (cent-levels)," one broker said.
Lean stocks and demand from Europe lifted October heating oil by 2.08 cents at the settle to 71.77 cents a gallon. The contract hit 72.25 cents on Wednesday, the highest since November 1991.
Traders said while prices for heating oil and crude could pull back early on Thursday, an upswing would resume later because of tight supplies.
"For the past seven API figures, stocks haven't built. In most ... they've actually shown a drawdown," a trader said.
Key support was seen at 70.00 cents for heating oil and around $23.75 a barrel for November crude.
NYMEX crude oil for November delivery traded at $23.36 a barrel by 0030 GMT on Thursday in overnight trade. That level was down 10 cents from the settle on a thin 286 lots.
Heating oil for October traded up 0.03 cent to 71.80 cents a gallon on a single lot.
Overall, distillates, which are used for heating oil and diesel, remain 19 million barrels below last year's levels at just over 38 million barrels.
October unleaded traded light, with levels seen at 63.00 cents a gallon, off 0.10 cent. Stock data showed imports up again, helping lift inventories by 3.06 million barrels last week.
Altogether 79 lots changed hands for front-month unleaded.
